prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you put ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Cookout Division.

I appear before this committee today not to evade, but to clarify. I understand the gravity of the allegations brought against me. To be accused of applying ketchup to a hot dog within the municipal boundaries of Chicago is not merely a culinary accusation; it is an accusation of cultural sedition. I do not take this lightly.

However, I must state for the record: **I am innocent of this charge.**

I have always maintained, and will continue to maintain, that a true Chicago-style hot dog is a sacred covenant. It is a vessel of yellow mustard, neon green sweet pickle relish, chopped white onions, tomato wedges, a dill pickle spear, sport peppers, and a dash of celery salt, all nestled within a steamed poppy seed bun. Ketchup has no place in this architecture. Its sweetness is an affront to the savory, spicy, and acidic balance that defines our great city’s street food heritage. To introduce ketchup is to introduce chaos. It is un-American in the most specific, geographical sense of the term.

If I have been seen reaching for a red bottle, let the record show it was for fries, or perhaps a burger, consumed at a safe and respectful distance from any encased meat product. I have never, knowingly or unknowingly, committed the act of ketchup-based desecration upon a Chicago dog.

I stand ready to answer any further questions regarding my condiment loyalty, my relish preferences, or my unwavering devotion to the sanctity of the Vienna Beef frankfurter. I yield my time, and my appetite, to the committee.
